becca-tarnas.name: Becca Tarnas
becca-tarnas.bio: Scholar of archetypal cosmology, Jung and Tolkien, teaching on the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred diploma.

peter-kingsley.name: Peter Kingsley
peter-kingsley.bio: Scholar of the Presocratics who reads Parmenides and Empedocles as mystics and healers, and writes on Jung's Red Book.

tom-cheetham.name: Tom Cheetham
tom-cheetham.bio: Philosopher and poet, the leading English-language interpreter of Henry Corbin and of the imaginal in Corbin and Hillman.

seyyed-hossein-nasr.name: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
seyyed-hossein-nasr.bio: Iranian philosopher of Islam and the perennial philosophy, a leading Traditionalist author and teacher of Chittick.

huston-smith.name: Huston Smith
huston-smith.bio: American scholar of world religions, author of The World's Religions and Forgotten Truth.

james-cutsinger.name: James S. Cutsinger
james-cutsinger.bio: American scholar of the perennial philosophy and Eastern Orthodox spirituality, editor of Schuon.

james-finley.name: James Finley
james-finley.bio: Clinical psychologist and former Trappist novice under Thomas Merton; CAC faculty and host of Turning to the Mystics.

louise-livingstone.name: Louise Livingstone
louise-livingstone.bio: Scholar of the heart and Goethean enquiry, co-founder of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019).

william-chittick.name: William C. Chittick
william-chittick.bio: Scholar and translator of Ibn Arabi and Rumi; doctorate at Tehran University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr (1974).

nazim-al-haqqani.name: Shaykh Nazim al-Haqqani
nazim-al-haqqani.bio: Turkish Cypriot Grand Shaykh of the Naqshbandi-Haqqani order.

geoffrey-cornelius.name: Geoffrey Cornelius
geoffrey-cornelius.bio: Astrologer and scholar of divination, co-creator of the Kent and Canterbury MAs in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

elliot-wolfson.name: Elliot R. Wolfson
elliot-wolfson.bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and Jewish philosophy; doctorate under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis (1986).

daniel-matt.name: Daniel C. Matt
daniel-matt.bio: Scholar of Kabbalah and translator of the Pritzker Edition of the Zohar; studied under Alexander Altmann at Brandeis.

prometheus-trust.name: The Prometheus Trust
prometheus-trust.bio: UK charity founded in 1986 by Tim Addey and others to keep the Platonic tradition alive as a way of life; publisher of the Thomas Taylor Series.

medina-tenour.name: Medina Tenour
medina-tenour.bio: Teacher on Sufi women saints and nature contemplation at the Rumi Center.

martin-lings.name: Martin Lings
martin-lings.bio: English Sufi author and Shakespeare scholar, disciple of Frithjof Schuon and onetime assistant to René Guénon in Cairo.

works.title: Muhammad: His Life Based on the Earliest Sources

rowan-williams.name: Rowan Williams
rowan-williams.bio: Theologian of Christian spirituality and former Archbishop of Canterbury (2002–2012).

mary-attwood.name: Mary Attwood
mary-attwood.bio: Art historian of the Renaissance imagination and director of the Centre for Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred.

william-stoddart.name: William Stoddart
william-stoddart.bio: Scottish Traditionalist author on Sufism and the perennial philosophy.

alireza-nurbakhsh.name: Alireza Nurbakhsh
alireza-nurbakhsh.bio: Master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order since 2008, succeeding his father Javad Nurbakhsh.

cyprian-consiglio.name: Cyprian Consiglio OSB Cam
cyprian-consiglio.bio: Camaldolese monk and musician teaching Christian meditation and interreligious contemplation.

mirabai-starr.name: Mirabai Starr
mirabai-starr.bio: Translator of the Spanish mystics and teacher of contemplative practice and grief.

embassy-curators.name: Embassy of the Free Mind curators
embassy-curators.bio: Curators of the Bibliotheca Philosophica Hermetica (Ritman Library) in Amsterdam, giving guided talks on its Hermetic and Böhme collections.

arthur-versluis.name: Arthur Versluis
arthur-versluis.bio: American scholar of Western esotericism and mysticism, founding editor of the journal Esoterica and author on Platonic mysticism and Gnosticism.

patrick-curry.name: Patrick Curry
patrick-curry.bio: Writer on enchantment, divination and ecology who taught on the Kent MA programme.

wouter-hanegraaff.name: Wouter J. Hanegraaff
wouter-hanegraaff.bio: Professor of History of Hermetic Philosophy and Related Currents at the University of Amsterdam and a founder of Western esotericism as an academic field.

simon-wilson.name: Simon Wilson
simon-wilson.bio: Canterbury Christ Church lecturer and course director of the MA in Myth, Cosmology and the Sacred (2019–2021).

frithjof-schuon.name: Frithjof Schuon
frithjof-schuon.bio: Metaphysician of the transcendent unity of religions and founder of the Maryamiyya Sufi order.

reza-shah-kazemi.name: Reza Shah-Kazemi
reza-shah-kazemi.bio: Scholar of comparative mysticism and Islamic spirituality.

jean-louis-michon.name: Jean-Louis Michon
jean-louis-michon.bio: French scholar of Sufism and Islamic art.

javad-nurbakhsh.name: Javad Nurbakhsh
javad-nurbakhsh.bio: Psychiatrist and master of the Nimatullahi Sufi Order for 55 years (1953–2008).

bernard-mcginn.name: Bernard McGinn
bernard-mcginn.bio: University of Chicago historian of Christian mysticism, author of the multi-volume The Presence of God.

christopher-titmuss.name: Christopher Titmuss
christopher-titmuss.bio: British insight meditation teacher, former Thai monk, who co-founded Gaia House in 1983.

christina-feldman.name: Christina Feldman
christina-feldman.bio: Insight meditation teacher and author who co-founded Gaia House in 1983 and is now one of its patrons.

stephen-batchelor.name: Stephen Batchelor
stephen-batchelor.bio: British former Tibetan and Zen monk, author of secular Buddhist books such as "Buddhism Without Beliefs"; long linked with Gaia House.

martine-batchelor.name: Martine Batchelor
martine-batchelor.bio: French former Korean Seon nun and meditation teacher, a patron of Gaia House.

lama-yeshe-losal.name: Lama Yeshe Losal Rinpoche
lama-yeshe-losal.bio: Akong Rinpoche's younger brother; retreat master of Samye Ling from 1988 and its abbot since 1995.

jiyu-kennett.name: Houn Jiyu-Kennett
jiyu-kennett.bio: English Soto Zen roshi trained at Sojiji who founded Shasta Abbey (1970), Throssel Hole (1972) and the Order of Buddhist Contemplatives.

daishin-morgan.name: Daishin Morgan
daishin-morgan.bio: Disciple of Jiyu-Kennett and abbot of Throssel Hole Buddhist Abbey from 1982 to 2019.

ajahn-khemadhammo.name: Ajahn Khemadhammo
ajahn-khemadhammo.bio: English disciple of Ajahn Chah who founded the Forest Hermitage in Warwickshire and the Angulimala prison chaplaincy.

sangharakshita.name: Sangharakshita
sangharakshita.bio: English monk (Dennis Lingwood) who founded the Triratna Buddhist Community (formerly FWBO) in London in 1967.

image.artist: The original uploader was Tathaataa at English Wikipedia.

pramukh-swami-maharaj.name: Pramukh Swami Maharaj
pramukh-swami-maharaj.bio: Guru and president of BAPS who inaugurated the Neasden mandir in 1995.

kelsang-gyatso.name: Kelsang Gyatso
kelsang-gyatso.bio: Tibetan lama who founded the New Kadampa Tradition and its mother centre at Conishead Priory, Cumbria.

sophrony-sakharov.name: Sophrony (Sakharov)
sophrony-sakharov.bio: Russian Orthodox elder, disciple and biographer of St Silouan the Athonite, who founded the monastery at Tolleshunt Knights in 1959.

julian-of-norwich.name: Julian of Norwich
julian-of-norwich.bio: English anchoress whose "Revelations of Divine Love" is the earliest surviving book in English known to be written by a woman.

george-fox.name: George Fox
george-fox.bio: English dissenter whose preaching from 1652 began the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers).

bulent-rauf.name: Bulent Rauf
bulent-rauf.bio: Turkish-born teacher around whom the Beshara School for the study of Ibn 'Arabi formed in the 1970s.

ibn-arabi.name: Ibn 'Arabi
ibn-arabi.bio: Andalusian Sufi master (1165-1240), "the greatest master", whose teaching on the unity of being shaped later Sufism.

inayat-khan.name: Inayat Khan
inayat-khan.bio: Indian musician and Sufi teacher who brought Sufism to the West, founding his order in London around 1914-1917.

ross-nichols.name: Ross Nichols
ross-nichols.bio: English poet and teacher who founded the Order of Bards, Ovates and Druids in 1964.

gerald-gardner.name: Gerald Gardner
gerald-gardner.bio: English civil servant who publicised the religion of Wicca from the 1950s.

doreen-valiente.name: Doreen Valiente
doreen-valiente.bio: English Wiccan priestess and poet, author of much of the Wiccan liturgy including the "Charge of the Goddess".

dion-fortune.name: Dion Fortune
dion-fortune.bio: British occultist (Violet Firth), founder of the Society (Fraternity) of the Inner Light and author of "The Mystical Qabalah".

image.artist: Author of this photo is unknown person.

aleister-crowley.name: Aleister Crowley
aleister-crowley.bio: English occultist, founder of Thelema, initiated in the Golden Dawn; owned Boleskine House.

samuel-liddell-macgregor-mathers.name: Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers
samuel-liddell-macgregor-mathers.bio: Co-founder of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn (1888) and translator of grimoires.

image.artist: The original uploader was Ihcoyc at English Wikipedia.

emma-restall-orr.name: Emma Restall Orr
emma-restall-orr.bio: English druid and writer who founded The Druid Network.

philip-carr-gomm.name: Philip Carr-Gomm
philip-carr-gomm.bio: Chosen Chief of OBOD from 1988 to 2020, pupil of Ross Nichols.

kathy-jones.name: Kathy Jones
kathy-jones.bio: Founder of the Glastonbury Goddess Temple and the Glastonbury Goddess Conference.

cecil-williamson.name: Cecil Williamson
cecil-williamson.bio: Founder of the Museum of Witchcraft, which settled in Boscastle in 1960.

karl-koenig.name: Karl König
karl-koenig.bio: Austrian paediatrician who founded the Camphill movement near Aberdeen in 1939-40.

douglas-harding.name: Douglas Harding
douglas-harding.bio: English philosopher whose "On Having No Head" launched the Headless Way.

christmas-humphreys.name: Christmas Humphreys
christmas-humphreys.bio: English barrister who founded the Buddhist Society in London in 1924.

john-crook.name: John Crook
john-crook.bio: British ethologist and Chan teacher, dharma heir of Sheng Yen, who founded the Western Chan Fellowship.

works.title: Creative Imagination in the Sufism of Ibn Arabi

freeTexts.title: On the Mysteries of the Egyptians, Chaldeans and Assyrians

francis-of-assisi.name: Francis of Assisi
francis-of-assisi.bio: Troubadour turned friar of Assisi; married Lady Poverty and preached to birds, sultans and lepers alike.

clare-of-assisi.name: Clare of Assisi
clare-of-assisi.bio: First follower of Francis and founder of the Poor Clares; kept the privilege of poverty against popes and cardinals.

bonaventure.name: Bonaventure
bonaventure.bio: Franciscan minister general who joined Aristotle to the mystical ascent: the soul's journey into God in six illuminations.

isaac-luria.name: Isaac Luria
isaac-luria.bio: Mystic of Safed whose two years of teaching (1569–1572) remade Kabbalah around tzimtzum, shevirat ha-kelim and tikkun.

hayyim-vital.name: Hayyim Vital
hayyim-vital.bio: Foremost disciple of Luria, whose notebooks (Etz Chaim) preserve nearly all we have of the master's teaching.

moinuddin-chishti.name: Muinuddin Chishti
moinuddin-chishti.bio: Founder of the Chishti order in India, settled in Ajmer; remembered for service to the poor and love without distinction.

nizamuddin-auliya.name: Nizamuddin Auliya
nizamuddin-auliya.bio: Chishti master of Delhi whose assemblies joined princes and paupers; Amir Khusrau was his foremost disciple.

amir-khusrau.name: Amir Khusrau
amir-khusrau.bio: Poet, musician and disciple of Nizamuddin; credited with shaping qawwali and Hindavi poetry at the Chishti court of Delhi.

abdul-qadir-gilani.name: Abdul Qadir Gilani
abdul-qadir-gilani.bio: Hanbali preacher and mystic of Baghdad whose teaching founded the Qadiri order, the first widespread Sufi order.

cornelius-agrippa.name: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa
cornelius-agrippa.bio: Author of the Three Books of Occult Philosophy, the Renaissance summa joining natural, celestial and ceremonial magic.

john-dee.name: John Dee
john-dee.bio: Mathematician, astrologer and angel-conversationalist to Elizabeth I; his Enochian workings with Edward Kelley defined English learned magic.

giordano-bruno.name: Giordano Bruno
giordano-bruno.bio: Dominican turned Hermetic philosopher, burned in Rome in 1600; read the infinite universe as the unfolding of the divine mind.

sayalay-dipankara.name: Sayalay Dipankara
sayalay-dipankara.bio: Pa-Auk-trained Burmese nun (b. 1964); teaches the 40 kammatthana and vipassana worldwide; founder/abbess of the Brahma Vihari centres.

ariyananda.name: Ven. Ariyananda
ariyananda.bio: Senior meditation teacher of Na Uyana Monastery; gives the weekly English Dhamma talks and retreat interviews in the Pa-Auk system.

dhammajiva.name: Uda Eriyagama Dhammajiva
dhammajiva.bio: Abbot and chief preceptor of Meetirigala Nissarana Vanaya; scholar-practitioner of samatha and vipassana, author of 40+ publications.

aggacitta.name: Ven. Aggacitta
aggacitta.bio: Malaysian monk; founder and guiding teacher of Sasanarakkha Buddhist Sanctuary (Taiping), answering the shortage of trained local monks.

thubten-chodron.name: Bhikshuni Thubten Chodron
thubten-chodron.bio: American-born Tibetan Buddhist nun (bhikshuni); founder and abbess of Sravasti Abbey; author and imprison-chaplaincy pioneer.

amma.name: Mata Amritanandamayi (Amma)
amma.bio: Hugging saint of Kerala; heads the Mata Amritanandamayi Math and its worldwide charities; gives darshan to millions.

mestre-irineu.name: Raimundo Irineu Serra (Mestre Irineu)
mestre-irineu.bio: Rubber-tapper turned prophet of Acre; founded the Santo Daime doctrine in the 1930s, weaving Christianity, shamanism and African spirit ways around the Daime sacrament.

mestre-gabriel.name: José Gabriel da Costa (Mestre Gabriel)
mestre-gabriel.bio: Rubber-tapper of Rondônia; founded the União do Vegetal, teaching love of God and neighbour through the hoasca sacrament; doctrine affirmed by the US Supreme Court (2006).

guru-nanak.name: Guru Nanak
guru-nanak.bio: Founder of Sikhism (1469–1539); taught one God, honest work and shared food; composed the Japji Sahib.

gobind-singh.name: Guru Gobind Singh
gobind-singh.bio: Tenth Sikh Guru; founded the Khalsa (1699), closed the human Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib.

yogi-bhajan.name: Yogi Bhajan
yogi-bhajan.bio: Brought Kundalini Yoga and Sikh Dharma to the West; founded the Espanola Mother Ashram (1970) and 3HO.

safety.summary: After December 2019 allegations (incl. Dyson's memoir), Yogi Bhajan's own organization commissioned An Olive Branch. Interviewing 299 people, the August 2020 report found it more likely than not that he engaged in sexual battery, sexual abuse, harassment and unethical conduct with 36 followers (1969–2004), with organizational enablers named. SSSC published it unedited.

reports.outlet: SSSC letter publishing the An Olive Branch report
Yoga Journal: A New Report Details Decades of Abuse

mahavira.name: Mahavira (Vardhamana)
mahavira.bio: 24th tirthankara (traditional dates); reformer of the Jain path; taught ahimsa and anekantavada in the Gangetic plain.

sushil-kumar.name: Acharya Sushil Kumarji
sushil-kumar.bio: Jain monk who carried Mahavira's message West from 1975; founded Siddhachalam (1983), the only Jain tirth outside India; taught Arhum Yoga. No successor.

laozi.name: Laozi
laozi.bio: Traditional author of the Daodejing (6th c. BCE, traditional); root figure of philosophical and religious Taoism.

bahaullah.name: Baha'u'llah
bahaullah.bio: Founder of the Baha'i Faith (1817–1892); Kitab-i-Aqdas; taught the oneness of God, religion and humanity.

abdu-l-baha.name: Abdu'l-Baha
abdu-l-baha.bio: Son and appointed successor of Baha'u'llah (1844–1921); spread the Faith in the West; no clergy — elected order.

sogyal-rinpoche.name: Sogyal Rinpoche
sogyal-rinpoche.bio: Founder of Rigpa; Tibetan teacher (Nyingma tulku) whose books reached millions; stepped back in 2017 after misconduct allegations, died 2019.

safety.summary: After a July 2017 letter from eight former students, Rigpa commissioned an independent investigation (Lewis Silkin, led by Karen Baxter). The August 2018 report found, on the balance of probabilities, that some inner-circle students were subjected to serious physical, sexual and emotional abuse, and that senior Rigpa figures knew of some issues and failed to act. Not all allegations were upheld. Rigpa published the report and its boards' response.

reports.outlet: UK Charity Commission inquiry: Rigpa Fellowship

sakyong-mipham.name: Sakyong Mipham Rinpoche
sakyong-mipham.bio: Head of the Shambhala lineage (son of Chögyam Trungpa); stepped back from teaching duties in 2018 after misconduct claims and investigation.

amrit-desai.name: Yogi Amrit Desai
amrit-desai.bio: Founder of Kripalu (1972); resigned 1994 after admitting affairs; federal litigation followed; Kripalu restructured without him.

kumaradza.name: Rigdzin Kumaradza
kumaradza.bio: Dzogchen master; root guru of Longchenpa (Vima Nyingthig) and teacher of the 3rd Karmapa Rangjung Dorje.

longchenpa.name: Longchen Rabjam (Longchenpa)
longchenpa.bio: Systematiser of Dzogchen (Seven Treasuries); successor of Kumaradza; visions of Padmasambhava; re-revealed by Jigme Lingpa centuries later.

jigme-lingpa.name: Jigme Lingpa
jigme-lingpa.bio: Tertön whose Longchen Nyingtik visions made Longchenpa's Heart Essence the dominant Nyingma practice cycle.

jigme-gyalwai-nyugu.name: Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu
jigme-gyalwai-nyugu.bio: Hermit of Dzachuka; heart-disciple of Jigme Lingpa and root guru of Patrul (ngöndro 25 times).

patrul.name: Patrul Rinpoche
patrul.bio: Wandering yogi-scholar; Words of My Perfect Teacher; root-guru lineage Jigme Lingpa→Gyalwai Nyugu→Patrul→Mipham.

mipham.name: Jamgon Mipham (Ju Mipham)
mipham.bio: Prolific Nyingma scholar (30+ volumes); student of Patrul, Kongtrul and Khyentse Wangpo; teacher of Shechen Gyaltsap; named infant Dilgo Khyentse.

jamgon-kongtrul.name: Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Thaye
jamgon-kongtrul.bio: Rimé collector (Five Treasuries) with Khyentse Wangpo and Chokgyur Lingpa; teacher of Mipham; emanation-source of Kalu Rinpoche's line.

jamyang-khyentse-wangpo.name: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
jamyang-khyentse-wangpo.bio: Tertön and Rimé founder with Kongtrul; root guru of Mipham; incarnation line continues (Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo, Dzongsar).

shechen-gyaltsap.name: Shechen Gyaltsap
shechen-gyaltsap.bio: Mipham's heart-disciple; root guru of Dilgo Khyentse (enthroned him as Khyentse Wangpo's mind emanation).

jamyang-khyentse-chokyi-lodro.name: Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö
jamyang-khyentse-chokyi-lodro.bio: Activity emanation of Khyentse Wangpo; second root teacher of Dilgo Khyentse; taught all four schools to 80+ masters' heir.

jigme-phuntsok.name: Khenchen Jigme Phuntsok
jigme-phuntsok.bio: Founder of Larung Gar (world's largest Buddhist institute); root guru of Khenpo Sodargye; nonsectarian tertön.

khamtrul-8.name: 8th Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima
khamtrul-8.bio: Drukpa master of Khampagar (Tashi Jong); root guru of Jetsunma Tenzin Palmo (ordained her 1964).

yonten-gyatso.name: Yonten Gyatso
yonten-gyatso.bio: Jonang throne-holder; gave Dolpopa the complete Kalachakra/Dro transmission and named him heir (1326).

huiguo.name: Huiguo
huiguo.bio: Tang court master at Qinglong Monastery; poured the two-mandala transmission into Kukai in months (805); 7th Shingon patriarch.

rendawa.name: Rendawa Zhonnu Lodro
rendawa.bio: Sakya master of explanation; Tsongkhapa's foremost teacher (Pramanavarttika, Madhyamaka); later mutual instruction.

phagmo-drupa.name: Phagmo Drupa Dorje Gyalpo
phagmo-drupa.bio: Gampopa's chief disciple; teacher of Jigten Sumgon; the eight Kagyu branches divide from his seat.

sachen.name: Sachen Kunga Nyingpo
sachen.bio: Founder of Sakya (1073); first of the Five Forefathers; father and first teacher of Dragpa Gyaltsen.

dragpa-gyaltsen.name: Jetsun Dragpa Gyaltsen
dragpa-gyaltsen.bio: Third Sakya patriarch; son and student of Sachen; principal teacher of his nephew Sakya Pandita.

sakya-pandita.name: Sakya Pandita Kunga Gyaltsen
sakya-pandita.bio: Fourth Sakya forefather; epistemologist (Treasury of Reasoning); student of Dragpa Gyaltsen and Sakya Shri; negotiated Tibet's surrender (1244).

tsangpa-gyare.name: Tsangpa Gyare
tsangpa-gyare.bio: Founder of the Drukpa Kagyu (student of Ling Repa); 'Thunder-Dragon' line of the Himalayas.

ling-repa.name: Lingchen Repa Pema Dorje
ling-repa.bio: Drukpa yogi; teacher of Tsangpa Gyare (medium confidence — confirm before treating as settled).

jigten-sumgon.name: Jigten Sumgon
jigten-sumgon.bio: Founder of Drikung Kagyu (Drikung Thil 1179); chief disciple of Phagmo Drupa; Gongchig (Single Intention).

niguma.name: Niguma
niguma.bio: Wisdom dakini of Kashmir; sister of Naropa; source of the Shangpa transmission to Khyungpo Naljor.

khyungpo-naljor.name: Khyungpo Naljor
khyungpo-naljor.bio: Founder of Shangpa Kagyu; seven India journeys; received Niguma/Sukhasiddhi transmissions; one-to-one lineage begins.

yizhin-norbu.name: Yizhin Norbu (Tsa Tsa Drubgen)
yizhin-norbu.bio: Abbot of Tsa Tsa Monastery; gave Kalu Rinpoche the complete Shangpa cycle in closed retreat (1940s).

khenchen-appey.name: Khenchen Appey Rinpoche
khenchen-appey.bio: Sakya scholar (International Buddhist Academy founder); teacher of senior Sakya masters including Dzongsar Khyentse.

rangjung-dorje.name: Rangjung Dorje (3rd Karmapa)
rangjung-dorje.bio: 3rd Karmapa; student of Kumaradza (Vima Nyingthig); discussed view with Dolpopa at Tsurphu (1321).

chenga-chokyi-gyalpo.name: Chenga Chokyi Gyalpo
chenga-chokyi-gyalpo.bio: Drikung patriarch under whom Tsongkhapa studied Mahamudra and the Six Dharmas of Naropa.

garab-dorje.name: Garab Dorje
garab-dorje.bio: First human holder of Dzogchen (traditional account); taught Mañjushrimitra; lineage root of the mind section.

manjushrimitra.name: Mañjushrimitra
manjushrimitra.bio: Second Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Garab Dorje, teacher of Shri Simha.

shri-simha.name: Shri Simha
shri-simha.bio: Third Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Mañjushrimitra, teacher of Jñanasutra.

jnanasutra.name: Jñanasutra
jnanasutra.bio: Fourth Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Shri Simha, teacher of Vimalamitra.

vimalamitra.name: Vimalamitra
vimalamitra.bio: Fifth Dzogchen holder (traditional); student of Jñanasutra; contemporary of Padmasambhava at Samye.

saraha.name: Saraha
saraha.bio: Mahasiddha of the doha songs; Mahamudra root figure; inspiration-line for Maitripa and Marpa's second transmission.

maitripa.name: Maitripa (Advayavajra)
maitripa.bio: Mahamudra master (1007–1085); Marpa's second guru after Naropa; Amanasikara cycle.

aryadeva.name: Aryadeva
aryadeva.bio: Nagarjuna's direct disciple; Four Hundred Verses; carried Madhyamaka to the south (and, traditionally, to Sri Lanka).

ronald-davidson.name: Ronald Davidson
ronald-davidson.bio: Fairfield historian of Indian esoteric Buddhism (Indian Esoteric Buddhism, Tibetan Renaissance); Vajrayana institutional history.

jayaratha.name: Jayaratha
jayaratha.bio: 13th-century Kashmir commentator whose Tantraloka-viveka unpacks Abhinavagupta's 37 chapters line by line.

yogaraja.name: Yogaraja
yogaraja.bio: Kashmir exegete; commentary on Abhinavagupta's Paramarthasara (Essence of the Highest Reality).

bhaskararaya.name: Bhaskararaya Makhin
bhaskararaya.bio: Sri Vidya polymath (1690–1785); Saubhagyabhaskara on the Lalita Sahasranama (1728), Setubandha (1748); initiated by Sivadatta Shukla at Surat.

sadyojyoti.name: Sadyojyoti
sadyojyoti.bio: Systematiser of Shaiva Siddhanta doctrine (c. 7th–9th c.); root figure of the dualist Shaiva schools.

meykandar.name: Meykandar
meykandar.bio: 13th-century Tamil philosopher; Sivajnanabodham (12 sutras); founded the Meykandar (Santana) Santana line via Paranjyoti's diksha.

paranjyoti.name: Paranjyoti Munivar
paranjyoti.bio: The sage 'descended from Kailash' who initiated the boy Meykandar on the street of Thiruvennainallur (traditional).

tirumular.name: Tirumular
tirumular.bio: Author of the Tirumantiram (3000 verses); among Nandinatha's eight disciples (traditional); Tamil Siddha root.

nandinatha.name: Nandinatha
nandinatha.bio: Legendary root guru of the Nandinatha Sampradaya; eight disciples incl. Tirumular (traditional).

sukhasiddhi.name: Sukhasiddhi
sukhasiddhi.bio: Wisdom dakini; student of Virupa; co-teacher (with Niguma) of Khyungpo Naljor's Shangpa transmission.

yajnavalkya.name: Yajnavalkya
yajnavalkya.bio: Upanishadic sage of the Brihadaranyaka; neti-neti dialogues with Maitreyi; debated by Gargi.

uddalaka.name: Uddalaka Aruni
uddalaka.bio: Father-teacher of Shvetaketu (Chandogya); 'Tat Tvam Asi' — thou art that.

shvetaketu.name: Shvetaketu
shvetaketu.bio: Uddalaka's son; received the nine homilies culminating in Tat Tvam Asi (Chandogya 6).

gargi.name: Gargi Vachaknavi
gargi.bio: Philosopher at Janaka's court; questioned Yajnavalkya on the woven-and-warped Brahman (Brihadaranyaka 3.6–3.8).

maitreyi.name: Maitreyi
maitreyi.bio: Yajnavalkya's wife-interlocutor; chose knowledge over wealth (Brihadaranyaka 2.4, 4.5).

nachiketa.name: Nachiketa
nachiketa.bio: Boy who questioned Death (Yama) and received the fire-doctrine and Self-knowledge (Katha Upanishad).

satyakama.name: Satyakama Jabala
satyakama.bio: Student of Haridrumata Gautama; truthfulness as qualification (Chandogya 4).

vashistha.name: Vashistha
vashistha.bio: Vedic seer (Rig Veda mandala 7); priest of Ikshvaku kings; Yoga-Vasishtha interlocutor.

vishvamitra.name: Vishvamitra
vishvamitra.bio: Seer of the Gayatri mantra (Rig Veda 3.62.10); rival-counterpart of Vashistha.

vyasa.name: Vyasa (Krishna Dvaipayana)
vyasa.bio: Traditional compiler of the Vedas and author of the Mahabharata; root figure of smriti.

valmiki.name: Valmiki
valmiki.bio: Traditional author of the Ramayana; 'first poet' (adikavi).

agastya.name: Agastya
agastya.bio: Vedic seer who carried the tradition south; Rig Vedic hymns + Tamil tradition root.

kallata.name: Kallaṭa
kallata.bio: Chief disciple of Vasugupta; received the Spanda-karika; bridge Vasugupta→Kashmir line.

rumi.name: Jalaluddin Rumi
rumi.bio: Persian poet-mystic (1207–1273); Divan and 25,000-verse Mathnawi; transformed by Shams (1244); order organized by son Sultan Walad.

shams-tabrizi.name: Shams-i Tabrizi
shams-tabrizi.bio: Wandering dervish whose 1244 Konya meeting transformed Rumi; Divan named for him; disappeared 1248 (traditional).

baha-walad.name: Baha al-Din Walad
baha-walad.bio: Rumi's father; Hanafi scholar-mystic of Balkh; family fled the Mongols to Konya; Rumi's first formation.

burhan-aldin.name: Sayyid Burhan al-Din
burhan-aldin.bio: Rumi's first Sufi master after his father (from 1232); nine years' training, forty-day retreats; directed his Aleppo studies.

sultan-walad.name: Sultan Walad
sultan-walad.bio: Rumi's son; first organizer of the Mevlevi order after Husam's death; Ibtidanama chronicler.

qunawi.name: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi
qunawi.bio: Ibn Arabi's stepson and foremost disciple (ijaza for all works); systematized the school (wujūd, Perfect Man); teacher of Tilimsani, Jandi, Iraqi.

plethon.name: Gemistus Plethon
plethon.bio: Byzantine Platonist of Mistra; Bessarion's teacher; Laws manuscript burned as pagan; Council of Florence catalyst.

bessarion.name: Basil Bessarion
bessarion.bio: Plethon's student turned cardinal; carried Plato west (In calumniatorem Platonis); exegetical schemes fed Ficino.

pico-della-mirandola.name: Giovanni Pico della Mirandola
pico-della-mirandola.bio: Florentine Academy junior; Oration on the Dignity of Man (900 theses); Christian Kabbalah with Ficino's Platonism.

augustine.name: Augustine of Hippo
augustine.bio: Bishop of Hippo (354–430); read the Platonists (Enneads in Latin); Confessions/City of God; baptized Neoplatonism into Christianity.

erigena.name: John Scottus Eriugena
erigena.bio: 9th-century Irish scholar at Laon; translated Pseudo-Dionysius into Latin; Periphyseon; channeled theosis west.

cusa.name: Nicholas of Cusa
cusa.bio: Cardinal-philosopher (1401–1464); learned ignorance (De docta ignorantia); Eckhart and Proclus/Dionysius debts.

parmenides.name: Parmenides
parmenides.bio: Presocratic of Elea (c. 515–450 BCE); the Way of Truth; read by the tradition (and Peter Kingsley) as mystic, not logician.

empedocles.name: Empedocles
empedocles.bio: Sicilian healer-prophet (c. 495–435 BCE); four roots + Love/Strife; mystic-physician of the Western root.

hsing-yun.name: Hsing Yun
hsing-yun.bio: Founder of Fo Guang Shan (1967) and 200+ branch temples incl. Nan Tien; Humanistic Buddhism.

swami-ramdev.name: Swami Ramdev
swami-ramdev.bio: Yoga teacher and Patanjali Yogpeeth co-founder; mass yoga camps, Ayurveda institutions.

shriram-sharma.name: Shriram Sharma Acharya
shriram-sharma.bio: Founder of Shantikunj/AWGP (1971); Gayatri sadhana, Yug Nirman mission; 3500+ centres.

chidanand-saraswati.name: Swami Chidanand Saraswati
chidanand-saraswati.bio: President of Parmarth Niketan; Ganga Aarti host; interfaith water/environment work.

ajahn-tong.name: Ajahn Tong Sirimangalo
ajahn-tong.bio: Mahasi student (Rangoon 1957); abbot of Chom Tong 1991–2019; spread four-foundations vipassana to 11+ countries; Northern Vipassana dept.

ajahn-martin.name: Ajahn Martin Piyadhammo
ajahn-martin.bio: German-born Thai Forest monk (Maha Bua line); Wat Phu Kong Tong; blunt desanas answered from practitioner questions; 3 free books.

ajahn-suphan.name: Ajahn Suphan
ajahn-suphan.bio: Abbot of Wat Ram Poeng (Tapotaram); carries Ajahn Tong's Northern Insight 26-day curriculum.

suhrawardi.name: Shihab al-Din Suhrawardi
suhrawardi.bio: Founder of Illuminationism (1154–1191, Aleppo); Hikmat al-Ishraq; light metaphysics; executed.

ghazali.name: Al-Ghazali
ghazali.bio: Theologian-mystic (1058–1111); Revival of the Religious Sciences; studied under al-Juwayni; Sufi turn after crisis.

hallaj.name: Mansur al-Hallaj
hallaj.bio: Ecstatic martyr (858–922, Baghdad); 'I am the Truth'; associated with Junayd's circle.

attar.name: Fariduddin Attar
attar.bio: Nishapur poet-pharmacist (c. 1145–1221); Conference of the Birds, Memorial of the Saints.

sanai.name: Sanai
sanai.bio: Ghazna court poet turned mystic (d. c. 1131); Hadiqa (Walled Garden), first great Persian Sufi mathnawi.

mulla-sadra.name: Mulla Sadra
mulla-sadra.bio: Safavid philosopher (1571–1640); transcendent theosophy (al-hikmah al-muta'aliyah); student of Mir Damad.

mir-damad.name: Mir Damad
mir-damad.bio: Safavid philosopher-scientist (d. 1631); teacher of Mulla Sadra; School of Isfahan.

juwayni.name: Al-Juwayni
juwayni.bio: Asharite theologian of Nishapur (1028–1085); Ghazali's master; Shafi'i authority.

junayd.name: Junayd al-Baghdadi
junayd.bio: Baghdad master (d. 910); sober Sufism; Hallaj moved in his circle and was reproved by him.

marinus.name: Marinus of Neapolis
marinus.bio: Successor of Proclus as head of the Athenian school; wrote the Life of Proclus.

aquinas.name: Thomas Aquinas
aquinas.bio: Dominican theologian (1225–1274); Summa; baptized Aristotle through Augustine's Platonist legacy.

chandrakirti.name: Chandrakirti
chandrakirti.bio: 7th-century Madhyamaka commentator (Madhyamakavatara); Prasangika reading of Nagarjuna.

shantideva.name: Shantideva
shantideva.bio: 8th-century monk-scholar; Bodhicaryavatara (Way of the Bodhisattva); taught by Patrul/Mipham line ever after.

vasubandhu.name: Vasubandhu
vasubandhu.bio: Abhidharmakosha author; converted to Mahayana by brother Asanga (traditional); Yogacara co-founder.

shantarakshita.name: Shantarakshita
shantarakshita.bio: Nalanda abbot invited to Tibet (8th c.); founded Samye with Padmasambhava; teacher of Kamalashila.

kamalashila.name: Kamalashila
kamalashila.bio: Disciple of Shantarakshita; Samye debate victor (traditional); Stages of Meditation.

taranatha.name: Jetsun Taranatha
taranatha.bio: Jonang historian-yogi (1575–1634); Damchö Ling founder; Kālacakra systematizer after Dolpopa.

yeshe-tsogyal.name: Yeshe Tsogyal
yeshe-tsogyal.bio: Padmasambhava's consort-disciple (8th c., traditional); treasure revealer; Nyingma mother-line root.

alara-kalama.name: Alara Kalama
alara-kalama.bio: Meditation teacher of the Bodhisatta (formless attainments); left unsatisfied for Uddaka, then alone.

uddaka-ramaputta.name: Uddaka Ramaputta
uddaka-ramaputta.bio: Second teacher of the Bodhisatta (neither-perception-nor-non-perception); declined, went forth alone.

arjun-seernels.name: Arjun Seernels
arjun-seernels.bio: Close student of Mark Dyczkowski who co-leads the Anuttara Trika Kula online Reading Circles on the Tantrāloka (from April 2026).

brian-campbell.name: Brian Campbell
brian-campbell.bio: Student of Mark Dyczkowski and Sanskritist who co-leads the Anuttara Trika Kula Reading Circles; announced Dyczkowski’s death and the completed Tantrāloka translation on the INDOLOGY list.

rameshwar-jha.name: Acharya Rameshwar Jha
rameshwar-jha.bio: Varanasi pandit and Kashmir Śaiva teacher under whom the young Mark Dyczkowski studied.

hemendra-chakravarti.name: Pandit Hemendra (Hemant) Nath Chakravarti
hemendra-chakravarti.bio: Varanasi scholar, disciple of Gopinath Kaviraj, editor of a Tantrasāra translation; teacher of Mark Dyczkowski from 1971.

gopinath-kaviraj.name: Gopinath Kaviraj
gopinath-kaviraj.bio: Varanasi Sanskrit scholar and Tantric adept, disciple of Vishuddhananda and close to Anandamayi Ma.

gurumayi-chidvilasananda.name: Gurumayi Chidvilasananda
gurumayi-chidvilasananda.bio: Head of Siddha Yoga who inaugurated the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute in 1997.

yogi-matsyendranath-maharaj.name: Guru Yogi Matsyendranath Maharaj (Matsyeshvarnath)
yogi-matsyendranath-maharaj.bio: Russian-born Nāth yogi who lived long among Nāths in India, received full initiation and guru status, and teaches Nāth haṭha and tantric sādhanā internationally through nathas.org.

yogi-lakshminath.name: Yogi Lakshminath Maharaj
yogi-lakshminath.bio: Teacher in the nathas.org community who leads online courses on prāṇāyāma, meditation, āsana and Śiva Sūtra satsangs.

yogi-allamanath.name: Yogi Allamanath
yogi-allamanath.bio: Teacher in the nathas.org community (tea satsangs and talks on the NathaChannel).

yogi-kamalnath.name: Yogi Kamalnath
yogi-kamalnath.bio: Main pujari of the Gorakhnath Mandir, Gorakhpur; teacher of Yogi Mithileshnath.

swami-sadatmananda.name: Swami Sadatmananda Saraswati
swami-sadatmananda.bio: Chief ācārya of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Anaikatti, since 2014 and paramount trustee of Sruti Seva Trust; trained under Swami Brahmatmananda (Baroda, 1986) and taught at Arsha Vidya Kendra Bangalore 1994–2014.

swami-brahmatmananda.name: Swami Brahmatmananda
swami-brahmatmananda.bio: Student of Swami Dayananda who ran a three-year Vedānta course in Baroda (1986) attended by Swami Sadatmananda.

swami-shankarananda-avg.name: Swami Shankarananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya)
swami-shankarananda-avg.bio: Disciple of Swami Dayananda teaching online Vedānta classes and retreats for AVG Anaikatti; ācārya of its Jan–Mar 2027 residential course. Distinct from Swami Shankarananda of Shiva Ashram (Kashmir Shaivism).

swami-sakshatkrtananda.name: Swami Sakshatkrtananda Saraswati
swami-sakshatkrtananda.bio: Senior Arsha Vidya teacher associated with Swami Dayananda Ashram, Rishikesh (listed in its About menu; ashram contact address sakshat1949@).

swamini-brahmaprakasananda.name: Mahamahopadhyaya Swamini Brahmaprakasananda Saraswati
swamini-brahmaprakasananda.bio: Senior disciple of Swami Dayananda and chief ācārya of Arsha Vijnana Gurukulam, Nagpur.

swamini-vedarthananda.name: Swamini Vedarthananda Saraswati
swamini-vedarthananda.bio: Faculty member at AVG Anaikatti who also looks after its temples.

swamini-saradananda.name: Swamini Saradananda Saraswati
swamini-saradananda.bio: Faculty member at AVG Anaikatti who also looks after its temples.

swami-muktatmananda.name: Swami Muktatmananda Saraswati
swami-muktatmananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher (Vedānta-sāra, Significance of OM series) at AVG Saylorsburg.

swami-sachidananda-avg.name: Swami Sachidananda (AVG)
swami-sachidananda-avg.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher and chanter at AVG Saylorsburg (Yoga of Objectivity series, satsangs).

swami-advayatmananda.name: Swami Advayatmananda
swami-advayatmananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher (Hastāmalakīyam course, guided meditations) at AVG Saylorsburg, 2025.

swami-pratyagbodhananda.name: Swami Pratyagbodhananda
swami-pratyagbodhananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher whose talks appear on the AVG channel.

swamini-paraprajnananda.name: Swamini Paraprajnananda
swamini-paraprajnananda.bio: Arsha Vidya teacher whose classes appear on the AVG channel.

swami-atmaswarupananda.name: Swami Atmaswarupananda
swami-atmaswarupananda.bio: Senior Divine Life Society monk who gives the morning meditation talks at the Christmas–New Year retreats, Sivananda Ashram.

swami-krishnananda.name: Swami Krishnananda
swami-krishnananda.bio: General secretary of the Divine Life Society for decades and prolific Vedānta lecturer (archival recordings).

kym-faculty.name: KYM faculty (Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram)
kym-faculty.bio: Collective teaching uploads of the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram: chanting, Dhanur-dhyāna sādhanā, prāṇa lecture series.

geshe-lhakdor.name: Geshe Lhakdor (Lobsang Jordhen)
geshe-lhakdor.bio: Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, former English translator to the Dalai Lama; teaches introductory Buddhism and Atiśa at LTWA.

tenzin-gache.name: Ven. Tenzin Gache
tenzin-gache.bio: FPMT teacher presenting Nāgārjuna’s Seventy Stanzas and Sixty Stanzas at Root Institute.

tenzin-legtsok.name: Ven. Tenzin Legtsok
tenzin-legtsok.bio: FPMT teacher ("Exploring the Mind Itself") at Root Institute.

geshe-tenzin-zopa.name: Geshe Tenzin Zopa
geshe-tenzin-zopa.bio: Gelug geshe teaching Atiśa’s Lamp for the Path and the Wheel of Sharp Weapons at Root Institute.

yogi-mithileshnath.name: Guru Yogi Mithileshnath Maharaj
yogi-mithileshnath.bio: Dharmanāth-panthī sadhu of Gorakhpur, student of Yogi Kamalnath and Yogi Dasharathnath, appointed head of the Nāth temple at Devi Patan in 2011; guru of Yogi Matsyendranath.

swami-charanashrit-giri.name: Swami (Sannyasi) Charanashrit Giri
swami-charanashrit-giri.bio: Founder-guru of Swara Yoga Peeth, Rishikesh; karma-sannyāsin of Paramahamsa Niranjanananda (Bihar School of Yoga), teaching the Śiva Svarodaya since 1993; titled Mahamandaleshwar in recent videos.

buddhism.label: Buddhism
buddhism.blurb: The path of the Buddha: seeing suffering, its cause in craving, and its ending, through virtue, meditation and wisdom.

theravada.label: Theravāda
theravada.blurb: The oldest surviving Buddhist school, rooted in the Pāli discourses and the monastic code; strong today in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

early-suttas.label: Early suttas
early-suttas.blurb: Practice read straight from the early discourses, outside the commentarial mainstream; Hillside Hermitage belongs here, drawing on Ñāṇavīra Thera.

thai-forest.label: Thai Forest
thai-forest.blurb: The forest monastic lineage of Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah.

insight.label: Insight meditation
insight.blurb: The modern vipassanā movement and its Western retreat centres.

mahayana.label: Mahāyāna
mahayana.blurb: The "great vehicle": the bodhisattva ideal of awakening for the sake of all beings, and the teaching of emptiness.

zen.label: Zen
zen.blurb: Chan and Zen: awakening through sitting, direct pointing and the teacher–student encounter, more than through scripture.

vajrayana.label: Vajrayāna
vajrayana.blurb: Tantric Buddhism: deity practice, mantra and the teacher's transmission as a swift path to awakening.

tibetan.label: Tibetan Buddhism
tibetan.blurb: The Buddhism of the Himalaya, joining monastic study and debate with Vajrayāna practice and guidance for the dying.

hindu.label: Hindu traditions
hindu.blurb: The many paths that grew from the Vedas and Upanishads: knowledge, devotion, yoga and action.

vedanta.label: Vedānta
vedanta.blurb: Philosophy built on the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gītā and the Brahma Sūtras, asking how the self relates to Brahman.

advaita.label: Advaita Vedānta
advaita.blurb: Non-dual Vedānta: the Self (ātman) is Brahman, and the world of separate selves is an appearance.

inchegeri.label: Inchegeri Sampradaya
inchegeri.blurb: The Navnath line of Siddharameshwar and Nisargadatta Maharaj.

ramakrishna-order.label: Ramakrishna Order
ramakrishna-order.blurb: The monastic order founded on Ramakrishna's teaching and Vivekananda's mission: Vedānta lived as service.

kashmir-shaivism.label: Kashmir Shaivism
kashmir-shaivism.blurb: A non-dual Tantric philosophy in which the world is the free, conscious play of Shiva, recognised as one's own self.

kriya-yoga.label: Kriya Yoga
kriya-yoga.blurb: The line of Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya and Paramahansa Yogananda.

christian.label: Christian traditions
christian.blurb: The traditions that follow Jesus of Nazareth, from the Gospels and the early Church to the mystics.

christian-mysticism.label: Christian mysticism
christian-mysticism.blurb: Christians who sought direct union with God: detachment, contemplative prayer and the birth of God in the soul.

gnosticism.label: Gnosticism
gnosticism.blurb: Early Christian and related movements of saving knowledge (gnosis); known mostly through texts such as the Nag Hammadi library.

platonic.label: Platonic tradition
platonic.blurb: Philosophy as the care of the soul, turning from the world of change toward the eternal Forms and the Good.

neoplatonism.label: Neoplatonism
neoplatonism.blurb: Late antique Platonism: everything flows from the One, and the soul can return to it through contemplation.

renaissance-platonism.label: Renaissance Platonism
renaissance-platonism.blurb: The revival of Plato and Plotinus in fifteenth-century Florence, joining Platonic philosophy with Christian faith.

esoteric.label: Western esotericism
esoteric.blurb: Western paths of hidden knowledge: Hermeticism, Theosophy, Anthroposophy and the Fourth Way.

theosophy.label: Theosophy
theosophy.blurb: The movement of Blavatsky and the Theosophical Society, joining Eastern ideas of karma and rebirth with Western occultism.

anthroposophy.label: Anthroposophy
anthroposophy.blurb: Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science: a path of clear thinking toward knowledge of spiritual worlds, karma and repeated earth lives.

fourth-way.label: The Fourth Way
fourth-way.blurb: Gurdjieff's path of self-remembering and conscious effort in the middle of ordinary life.

independent.label: Independent
independent.blurb: Teachers who stand outside any tradition.

direct-path.label: Direct path
direct-path.blurb: The non-dual enquiry into experience taught by Atmananda Krishna Menon and carried on by Jean Klein, Francis Lucille and Rupert Spira.

arsha-vidya.label: Arsha Vidya
arsha-vidya.blurb: Traditional teaching of Advaita Vedanta through the texts, in the line of Swami Dayananda Saraswati (Arsha Vidya Gurukulam, Q4796497).

modern-nondual.label: Modern non-dual teachers
modern-nondual.blurb: Contemporary teachers of awakening who draw on Zen, Advaita and other sources without belonging to one lineage.

plum-village.label: Plum Village
plum-village.blurb: Thich Nhat Hanh's Vietnamese Thiền community of engaged, mindful living.

soto-zen.label: Sōtō Zen
soto-zen.blurb: Dōgen's school of just-sitting (shikantaza); San Francisco Zen Center, Sanshin.

rinzai-zen.label: Rinzai Zen
rinzai-zen.blurb: The koan school of Japanese Zen; Zen Studies Society.

gelug.label: Gelug
gelug.blurb: The Tibetan school of Tsongkhapa, headed in practice by the Dalai Lamas.

burmese.label: Burmese meditation lineages
burmese.blurb: Myanmar's modern meditation schools: Mahasi noting, Pa-Auk samatha-vipassanā, U Ba Khin and Goenka.

krishnamurti.label: Krishnamurti
krishnamurti.blurb: J. Krishnamurti's teaching after he left Theosophy in 1929: no path, no authority, freedom from the known.

anandamayi-sangha.label: Anandamayi Ma Sangha
anandamayi-sangha.blurb: The ashrams and monastics around Anandamayi Ma (Shree Shree Anandamayee Sangha, Kankhal and Varanasi), devotional and non-sectarian.

divine-life-society.label: Divine Life Society
divine-life-society.blurb: The order founded by Swami Sivananda in Rishikesh, carried on by Swami Chidananda.

siddha-yoga.label: Siddha Yoga
siddha-yoga.blurb: Guru-yoga path founded by Swami Muktananda in the line of Bhagawan Nityananda: shaktipat, chanting and meditation, drawing on Kashmir Shaiva texts.

goenka-vipassana.label: Goenka Vipassana (U Ba Khin line)
goenka-vipassana.blurb: Lay Vipassana in the line of Ledi Sayadaw, Saya Thetgyi and U Ba Khin, taught by S. N. Goenka in 10-day dana-funded courses.

kagyu.label: Kagyu
kagyu.blurb: Tibetan school of the mahamudra lineage from Tilopa and Naropa through Marpa and Milarepa, led by the Karmapas.

nyingma.label: Nyingma
nyingma.blurb: The oldest Tibetan school, tracing to Padmasambhava, home of Dzogchen.

sufism.label: Sufism
sufism.blurb: The inner, mystical path of Islam: remembrance of God (dhikr), the master and the order, the poetry of love.

jewish.label: Jewish mysticism
jewish.blurb: Merkavah, Kabbalah, the Zohar and Hasidism: the contemplative and mystical currents of Judaism.

philosophy-of-the-sacred.label: Philosophy of the sacred
philosophy-of-the-sacred.blurb: Contemporary philosophers and scientists on consciousness, meaning and the sacred: idealism, the divided brain, the meaning crisis, perennialism.

modern-paganism.label: Modern Paganism
modern-paganism.blurb: Druidry, Wicca, Heathenry and goddess spirituality: nature-centred traditions revived or founded in the modern era.

sikh.label: Sikhism
sikh.blurb: The path of the ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib: remembrance of the one Name, honest work and sharing.

shaivism.label: Śaivism
shaivism.blurb: Umbrella for Śiva-centred traditions: the ascetic Atimārga and the initiatory Mantramārga.

pashupata.label: Pāśupata (Atimārga)
pashupata.blurb: Earliest Śaiva ascetic order; ash, feigned madness, provoking censure.

shaiva-siddhanta.label: Śaiva Siddhānta
shaiva-siddhanta.blurb: Mainstream ritual Śaivism of the Mantramārga; Sanskrit āgamas, later the Tamil Śaiva temple tradition. Kauai Aadheenam teaches a monistic form.

trika.label: Trika
trika.blurb: Abhinavagupta's synthesis around the Mālinīvijayottara; Tantrāloka.

pratyabhijna.label: Pratyabhijñā (Recognition)
pratyabhijna.blurb: Philosophical school: liberation as recognising oneself as Śiva.

spanda.label: Spanda (Vibration)
spanda.blurb: Śiva Sūtras and Spanda Kārikās: consciousness as pulsation.

krama.label: Krama / Kālīkula (Mahārtha)
krama.blurb: Kālī-centred phases (krama) of cognition; Twelve Kālīs.

shaktism.label: Śāktism
shaktism.blurb: Goddess-centred traditions; parent of Kaula, Śrī Vidyā and Kālī lines.

shakta.label: Śākta practice (Kālī, Kāmākhyā, Bhairavī)
shakta.blurb: Bucket for living goddess practice not tied to a single classical school (Kāmākhyā upāsanā, Linga Bhairavi, Daśa Mahāvidyā).

sri-vidya.label: Śrī Vidyā
sri-vidya.blurb: Worship of Lalitā Tripurasundarī through the Śrī Chakra and the fifteen-syllable mantra.

siddha-siddhanta.label: Nāth / Siddha Siddhānta
siddha-siddhanta.blurb: Nāth yogī order (Gorakhnāth); Siddha Siddhānta Paddhati; alchemy and haṭha.

hatha.label: Haṭha Yoga (premodern)
hatha.blurb: Physical-yogic methods first set out in Vajrayāna and Śaiva circles (Amṛtasiddhi, Dattātreyayogaśāstra, Haṭhapradīpikā).

tantra-studies.label: Tantra studies (academic)
tantra-studies.blurb: Not a tradition: a field tag for scholarly lectures (philology, history).

chah-line.label: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)
chah-line.blurb: Includes Amaravati, Chithurst/Cittaviveka, Abhayagiri, Bodhinyana/BSWA, Wat Pah Nanachat, Wat Marp Jan, Wat Boonyawad, Tisarana, Birken.

mun-boowa-line.label: Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)
mun-boowa-line.blurb: Note: Ajahn Dtun, listed by the brief under this line, was ordained by Ajahn Chah (Mahānikāya) and is filed under chah-line.

pa-auk.label: Pa-Auk (samatha-first, Abhidhamma)
pa-auk.blurb: No usable official English short talks found this pass.

mogok.label: Mogok Sayadaw (dependent origination)
mogok.blurb: Official channel is Burmese-language only; no English clips.

sri-lankan.label: Sri Lankan Theravāda (forest & scholastic)
sri-lankan.blurb: Hillside Hermitage is already deep in app (early-suttas).

buddhist-studies.label: Buddhist studies (academic)
buddhist-studies.blurb: Scholarly lineage node: edges are academic_supervisor_of.

sivananda-yoga.label: Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres
sivananda-yoga.blurb: Swami Vishnudevananda's international centres teaching his guru Sivananda's yoga.

bihar-yoga.label: Bihar School of Yoga (Satyananda Yoga)
bihar-yoga.blurb: Yoga of Swami Satyananda, disciple of Sivananda, and the Bihar School of Yoga.

gaudiya.label: Gaudiya Vaishnava (Chaitanya / ISKCON)
gaudiya.blurb: Krishna devotion in the line of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

dzogchen.label: Dzogchen (Great Perfection)
dzogchen.blurb: Teaching and practice lineage, not a separate institution; also held in Bön and taught across Rimé.

karma-kagyu.label: Karma Kagyu
karma-kagyu.blurb: Largest Kagyu branch, led by the Karmapas.

shangpa-kagyu.label: Shangpa Kagyu
shangpa-kagyu.blurb: Separate lineage from Niguma and Sukhasiddhi, revived by Kalu Rinpoche.

mahamudra.label: Mahamudra (the Great Seal)
mahamudra.blurb: Practice lineage at the heart of Kagyu, also taught in Gelug.

sakya.label: Sakya
sakya.blurb: Lamdre (path and its fruit) teachings; led by the Khön family.

fpmt.label: FPMT (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition)
fpmt.blurb: International Gelug network founded by Lama Yeshe and Lama Zopa.

jonang.label: Jonang
jonang.blurb: Known for shentong (other-emptiness) and Kalachakra; suppressed in central Tibet in the 17th c. and survives in Amdo.

bon.label: Bön (Yungdrung Bön)
bon.blurb: Tibet's indigenous religion. It is not a Buddhist school, but it shares its institutions and Dzogchen with Buddhism. Placed here for browsing only.

rime.label: Rimé (non-sectarian) movement
rime.blurb: An ecumenical revival across Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Jonang, not a school.

shambhala.label: Shambhala
shambhala.blurb: Trungpa's secular "warrior" path; Pema Chödrön trained in it.

chan.label: Chan
chan.blurb: Chinese meditation school, root of Zen, Seon and Thiền.

dharma-drum.label: Dharma Drum Mountain
dharma-drum.blurb: Taiwanese Chan organisation of Sheng Yen holding both Linji and Caodong lines.

sanbo-zen.label: Sanbo Zen (Sanbo Kyodan)
sanbo-zen.blurb: Lay-oriented school combining Soto and Rinzai koan curricula.

white-plum.label: White Plum Asanga
white-plum.blurb: Maezumi's lineage network (Soto with Rinzai koan study).

seon.label: Seon (Korean Zen)
seon.blurb: Korean Chan; Jogye order; Kwan Um School in the West.

kwan-um.label: Kwan Um School of Zen
kwan-um.blurb: International Seon school of Seung Sahn.

plum-village-thien.label: Thiền
plum-village-thien.blurb: Vietnamese Chan; Plum Village is its best-known modern form.

ocb.label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives
ocb.blurb: Shasta Abbey tradition founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

tiantai.label: Tiantai
tiantai.blurb: Lotus Sutra school; threefold truth; zhiguan (calming and contemplation).

tendai.label: Tendai
tendai.blurb: Japanese Tiantai, which also includes esoteric (taimitsu), Pure Land and Zen elements.

huayan.label: Huayan (Kegon)
huayan.blurb: Avatamsaka school; interpenetration of all phenomena.

pure-land.label: Pure Land
pure-land.blurb: Devotion to Amitabha and rebirth in Sukhavati.

jodo-shinshu.label: Jōdo Shinshū (Shin Buddhism)
jodo-shinshu.blurb: Shinran's school; Buddhist Churches of America in the US.

east-asian-esoteric.label: East Asian esoteric Buddhism
east-asian-esoteric.blurb: Chinese Zhenyan and its Japanese heirs.

western-magic.label: Western magic
western-magic.blurb: Ritual and initiatory magic in the Hermetic and Qabalistic line: the Golden Dawn, Thelema, the Inner Light.

akbarian.label: Akbarian school (Ibn Arabi)
akbarian.blurb: Study and practice centred on Ibn 'Arabi's teaching of the unity of being, as at Beshara.

naqshbandi.label: Naqshbandi-Haqqani order
naqshbandi.blurb: Sufi order known for silent remembrance (dhikr) and tracing its chain through Abu Bakr.

inayati.label: Inayatiyya (universal Sufism, Chishti roots)
inayati.blurb: Universal Sufism of Hazrat Inayat Khan, founded in London around 1914-1917.

christian-meditation-wccm.label: Christian Meditation (John Main / WCCM)
christian-meditation-wccm.blurb: Contemplative prayer with a single prayer word, taught by John Main and the World Community for Christian Meditation.

franciscan.label: Franciscan contemplative (Rohr / CAC)
franciscan.blurb: Followers of St Francis; in the UK including the Anglican Society of St Francis.

hesychasm.label: Orthodox hesychasm
hesychasm.blurb: Eastern Orthodox prayer of inner stillness and the Jesus Prayer.

kabbalah.label: Kabbalah (theosophical and ecstatic)
kabbalah.blurb: Jewish mystical tradition of the sefirot and the hidden meanings of Torah; also its modern popular forms.

druidry.label: Druidry
druidry.blurb: Modern Druid spirituality of nature, the seasonal festivals and bardic arts, as in OBOD.

wicca.label: Wicca
wicca.blurb: Modern pagan witchcraft publicised by Gerald Gardner from the 1950s, with covens, the Goddess and God and the wheel of the year.

heathenry.label: Heathenry
heathenry.blurb: Modern revival of pre-Christian Germanic and Norse religion (Asatru, Odinism).

goddess-spirituality.label: Goddess spirituality
goddess-spirituality.blurb: Devotion to the divine feminine as Goddess, centred in the UK on Glastonbury.

golden-dawn.label: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
golden-dawn.blurb: Initiatory order founded in London in 1888 that shaped modern Western magic.

thelema.label: Thelema
thelema.blurb: Aleister Crowley's religious and magical system ("Do what thou wilt").

quaker.label: Quakers (Religious Society of Friends)
quaker.blurb: Christian movement begun by George Fox in 1652, worshipping in expectant silence.

benedictine.label: Benedictine monasticism
benedictine.blurb: Monastic life under the Rule of St Benedict.

cistercian.label: Cistercians (Trappists)
cistercian.blurb: Reformed Benedictines; Trappists are the Strict Observance.

carmelite.label: Carmelites
carmelite.blurb: Contemplative order of Teresa of Avila and John of the Cross.

ignatian.label: Ignatian spirituality
ignatian.blurb: The Jesuit way of the Spiritual Exercises of Ignatius of Loyola.

celtic-christianity.label: Celtic Christianity
celtic-christianity.blurb: The early Christianity of Britain and Ireland (Columba, Aidan, Cuthbert, David) and its modern revival.

triratna.label: Triratna Buddhist Community
triratna.blurb: Western Buddhist movement founded by Sangharakshita in London in 1967 (formerly FWBO).

new-kadampa.label: New Kadampa Tradition
new-kadampa.blurb: Movement founded by Kelsang Gyatso in England, presenting itself as independent of the Tibetan schools (Gelug-derived; contested).

serene-reflection.label: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives (Serene Reflection)
serene-reflection.blurb: Soto Zen order founded by Jiyu-Kennett, seated at Shasta Abbey and Throssel Hole.

nipponzan-myohoji.label: Nipponzan-Myohoji
nipponzan-myohoji.blurb: Japanese Nichiren order of Nichidatsu Fujii that builds peace pagodas.

iskcon.label: ISKCON (Hare Krishna)
iskcon.blurb: International Society for Krishna Consciousness, founded by A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada in 1966.

swaminarayan.label: Swaminarayan Sampradaya
swaminarayan.blurb: Vaishnava tradition of Swaminarayan, including BAPS.

brahma-kumaris.label: Brahma Kumaris
brahma-kumaris.blurb: Spiritual movement founded in Sindh in the 1930s, teaching Raja Yoga meditation; headquarters at Mount Abu.

transcendental-meditation.label: Transcendental Meditation
transcendental-meditation.blurb: Mantra meditation of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi.

swedenborgian.label: Swedenborgianism
swedenborgian.blurb: Thought and church following the visions of Emanuel Swedenborg.

spiritualism.label: Spiritualism
spiritualism.blurb: Movement based on communication with the dead through mediums.

kaula.label: Kaula / Kula
kaula.blurb: Clan (kula) cults of yoginīs and Bhairava; source of many later Śākta and haṭha practices.

franciscan-contemplative.label: Franciscan contemplative
franciscan-contemplative.blurb: The Franciscan contemplative current: poverty and minority as a way of seeing, from Francis and Clare through Bonaventure to today.

lurianic.label: Lurianic Kabbalah
lurianic.blurb: The Kabbalah of Isaac Luria as recorded by Hayyim Vital: contraction (tzimtzum), the breaking of the vessels, and repair (tikkun).

chishti.label: Chishti order
chishti.blurb: The Sufi order of Muinuddin Chishti, rooted in Ajmer: music (sama, qawwali), service of the poor, and love of the teacher.

qadiri.label: Qadiri order
qadiri.blurb: The Sufi order of Abdul Qadir Gilani of Baghdad: sober adherence to the law joined to inward poverty and reliance on God.

learned-magic.label: Learned magic
learned-magic.blurb: Renaissance learned magic: Ficino's Neoplatonic natural magic, Agrippa's three books, Dee's angelic conversations, Bruno's heroic frenzies. Studied, not practised, here.

shamanic.label: Shamanic traditions
shamanic.blurb: Shamanic and plant-medicine healing traditions of the Americas, entered only where lineage, teachers and screening are verifiable.

santo-daime.label: Santo Daime
santo-daime.blurb: Syncretic Amazonian religion founded by Raimundo Irineu Serra (1930s): Christianity, South American shamanism, African animism, Kardecist spiritism. Legal churches in Oregon, Los Angeles, Washington.

udv.label: União do Vegetal (UDV)
udv.blurb: Christian Spiritist religion founded by José Gabriel da Costa; hoasca sacrament; US Supreme Court exemption 2006 (Gonzales v. O Centro). Núcleos across the US.

shipibo-curanderismo.label: Shipibo curanderismo
shipibo-curanderismo.blurb: Shipibo-Conibo plant-spirit healing (curanderismo): onanya healers, ikaros songs, dietas. Entered via its longest-running centre, not via individual claims.

jain.label: Jainism
jain.blurb: The Jain dharma: non-violence (ahimsa), non-possessiveness and many-sidedness (anekantavada) on the tirthankara path.

taoist.label: Taoism
taoist.blurb: The Chinese Way: Daodejing and Zhuangzi, inner alchemy, ritual and martial lineages (Quanzhen, Zhengyi, Wudang).

bahai.label: Baha'i Faith
bahai.blurb: The Baha'i Faith: unity of God, religion and humanity; no clergy, elected assemblies; Houses of Worship open to all.

african-diaspora.label: African diaspora religions
african-diaspora.blurb: African diaspora religions of the Americas, entered only via heritage-listed houses with published contacts.

candomble.label: Candomblé
candomble.blurb: Ketu-nation Candomblé of Bahia: orixá worship, entered via the IPHAN-listed Ilê Axé Opô Afonjá (1910).

native-american-church.label: Native American Church
native-american-church.blurb: The peyote way of the North American tribes; pan-tribal church body (NACNA). Tribally rooted, not drop-in.

rigpa.label: Rigpa
rigpa.blurb: Worldwide Buddhist network founded by Sogyal Rinpoche (Nyingma roots); commissioned the 2018 independent investigation into its founder.

drukpa.label: Drukpa Kagyu
drukpa.blurb: Drukpa (Thunder-Dragon) Kagyu of Tsangpa Gyare; Himalayan stronghold (Bhutan, Ladakh, Lahaul).

drikung.label: Drikung Kagyu
drikung.blurb: Drikung Kagyu of Jigten Sumgon; Gongchig and Fivefold Mahamudra; Drikung Thil.

shangpa.label: Shangpa Kagyu
shangpa.blurb: Shangpa Kagyu of Niguma and Khyungpo Naljor; the 'secret lineage', one-to-one transmission; Kalu Rinpoche its modern holder.

madhyamaka.label: Madhyamaka
madhyamaka.blurb: Middle-Way philosophy of Nagarjuna and Aryadeva: emptiness (shunyata) via the tetralemma; root of Mahayana dialectics and, through Chandrakirti, of Tibetan debate.

vedic.label: Vedic
vedic.blurb: Vedic religion: Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, principal Upanishads; Rishis and the Yajnavalkya dialogues that Vedanta inherits.

contemplating-not-self.name: Contemplating not-self
contemplating-not-self.summary: Take each aggregate in turn and ask: is it constant, is it easeful, is it fitting to regard it as me, mine, my self?

steps.text: Take each aggregate in turn and ask: is it constant, is it easeful, is it fitting to regard it as me, mine, my self?

shiva-process-self-inquiry.name: Shiva Process self-inquiry
shiva-process-self-inquiry.summary: Bring to mind a situation that is troubling you. Describe what you feel in plain words, then ask "what is the deeper feeling under this?" and keep going, layer by layer, until something shifts and the contraction releases. Often done in pairs or with a guide.

steps.text: Bring to mind a situation that is troubling you.
Describe what you feel in plain words, then ask "what is the deeper feeling under this?" and keep going, layer by layer, until something shifts and the contraction releases.

what-am-i-don-t-know.name: "What am I? Don't know"
what-am-i-don-t-know.summary: Ask "What am I?" deeply on the in-breath. On the out-breath, hold "Don't know..." as long as the breath lasts. Return to this don't-know mind in every activity, and keep clear about the next correct action. This is Seung Sahn's Kwan Um teaching.

steps.text: Ask "What am I?" deeply on the in-breath.
On the out-breath, hold "Don't know..." as long as the breath lasts.
Return to this don't-know mind in every activity, and keep clear about the next correct action.

contraindications: Keep the breath natural and unforced. Stop if you feel dizzy, anxious or unwell.

owner-of-my-actions.name: Owner of my actions
owner-of-my-actions.summary: The fifth remembrance: I am the owner of my actions, heir to my actions. Recollect it before acting and after.

steps.text: The fifth remembrance: I am the owner of my actions, heir to my actions.
Recollect it before acting and after.

mindfulness-of-breathing.name: Mindfulness of breathing
mindfulness-of-breathing.summary: Sit comfortably, know the in-breath and out-breath, then let the breath calm the whole body before turning to feelings and mind.

steps.text: Sit comfortably, know the in-breath and out-breath, then let the breath calm the whole body before turning to feelings and mind.

contraindications: Keep the breath natural and unforced. Stop if you feel dizzy, anxious or unwell.

goodwill-metta.name: Goodwill (metta)
goodwill-metta.summary: Wish yourself well, then widen the wish to others, near and far, seen and unseen, without exception.

steps.text: Wish yourself well, then widen the wish to others, near and far, seen and unseen, without exception.

resting-in-the-gap-between-breaths-vijna.name: Resting in the gap between breaths (Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā)
resting-in-the-gap-between-breaths-vijna.summary: Sit comfortably and breathe naturally. Notice the instant where the in-breath turns into the out-breath, and the instant where the out-breath turns back. Do not hold the breath; simply let attention fall into each turning point and rest there for its brief duration. Over time, notice the open awareness that is present in the pause.

steps.text: Sit comfortably and breathe naturally.
Notice the instant where the in-breath turns into the out-breath, and the instant where the out-breath turns back.
Do not hold the breath; simply let attention fall into each turning point and rest there for its brief duration.
Over time, notice the open awareness that is present in the pause.

contraindications: Keep the breath natural and unforced. Stop if you feel dizzy, anxious or unwell.

sources.cite: Bettina Bäumer, Vijñāna Bhairava verses 24–27 (the breath dhāraṇās).

recognition-pratyabhijna-contemplation.name: Recognition (pratyabhijñā) contemplation
recognition-pratyabhijna-contemplation.summary: Read one sūtra of the Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam slowly. Then look at present experience — a sound, a thought, a feeling — and ask whether anything appears outside awareness. Let the understanding "this too is a form of the one consciousness" settle as a felt recognition rather than an idea. Return to the text, then to experience, alternating.

steps.text: Read one sūtra of the Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam slowly.
Then look at present experience — a sound, a thought, a feeling — and ask whether anything appears outside awareness.
Let the understanding "this too is a form of the one consciousness" settle as a felt recognition rather than an idea.
Return to the text, then to experience, alternating.

sources.cite: Christopher Wallis on the twenty sūtras of the Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam.

drawing-the-sri-chakra-as-meditation.name: Drawing the Śrī Chakra as meditation
drawing-the-sri-chakra-as-meditation.summary: Following a teacher's step-by-step construction, draw the Śrī Yantra slowly from the centre point (bindu) outward: the nine interlocking triangles, the lotus rings and the square gateways. Treat each stage as a contemplation of the goddess unfolding into the world, not as geometry homework.

steps.text: Following a teacher's step-by-step construction, draw the Śrī Yantra slowly from the centre point (bindu) outward: the nine interlocking triangles, the lotus rings and the square gateways.
Treat each stage as a contemplation of the goddess unfolding into the world, not as geometry homework.

sources.cite: Devipuram, "How to Draw Sri Chakra" parts 1–2.

basic-saiva-siddhanta-meditation.name: Basic Śaiva Siddhānta meditation
basic-saiva-siddhanta-meditation.summary: Sit upright, regulate the breath to a slow even count, then draw awareness inward from the senses to the spine and to the inner light, holding a single point of focus. Hinduism Today's monastery teaches it as part of daily worship and study.

steps.text: Sit upright, regulate the breath to a slow even count, then draw awareness inward from the senses to the spine and to the inner light, holding a single point of focus.
Hinduism Today's monastery teaches it as part of daily worship and study.

contraindications: Keep the breath natural and unforced. Stop if you feel dizzy, anxious or unwell.

sources.cite: Bodhinatha Veylanswami, "How Do We Meditate? Part 1".

mantra-repetition-japa.name: Mantra repetition (japa)
mantra-repetition-japa.summary: Choose a mantra received from your tradition, sit with a mala, and repeat it at an even pace, aloud, whispered or mentally. Let attention rest on the sound and its meaning; when the mind wanders, return to the next repetition.

steps.text: Choose a mantra received from your tradition, sit with a mala, and repeat it at an even pace, aloud, whispered or mentally.
Let attention rest on the sound and its meaning; when the mind wanders, return to the next repetition.

anapanasati-breath-meditation-method-2.name: Ānāpānasati (breath meditation, "Method 2")
anapanasati-breath-meditation-method-2.traditionLabel: Dhammayut forest line (Ajahn Mun → Maha Boowa / Ajaan Lee)
anapanasati-breath-meditation-method-2.summary: Sit upright and notice the breath at whatever point it is clearest. Let it settle into a comfortable rhythm, then let that sense of ease spread through the whole body, using the breath energy as a home base for steady, alert attention.

steps.text: Sit upright and notice the breath at whatever point it is clearest.
Let it settle into a comfortable rhythm, then let that sense of ease spread through the whole body, using the breath energy as a home base for steady, alert attention.

contraindications: Keep the breath natural and unforced. Stop if you feel dizzy, anxious or unwell.

buddho-recollection.name: "Buddho" recollection
buddho-recollection.summary: Silently repeat "bud-" on the in-breath and "-dho" on the out-breath to anchor the mind; when the mind is calm, drop the word and stay with the knowing itself. Used widely in the Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah lines.

steps.text: Silently repeat "bud-" on the in-breath and "-dho" on the out-breath to anchor the mind; when the mind is calm, drop the word and stay with the knowing itself.

walking-meditation-jongrom.name: Walking meditation (jongrom)
walking-meditation-jongrom.traditionLabel: Ajahn Chah line (Wat Nong Pah Pong)
walking-meditation-jongrom.summary: Choose a straight path of 15–30 paces. Walk at a natural or slow pace, attention on the feet or the whole body; at each end, stop, turn, and re-collect before walking back.

steps.text: Choose a straight path of 15–30 paces.
Walk at a natural or slow pace, attention on the feet or the whole body; at each end, stop, turn, and re-collect before walking back.

mahasi-noting.name: Mahasi noting
mahasi-noting.summary: Watch the rise and fall of the abdomen and give each event a soft mental label ("rising", "falling", "thinking", "hearing"), then return to the primary object; move to slow walking with labels for lifting, moving and placing.

steps.text: Watch the rise and fall of the abdomen and give each event a soft mental label ("rising", "falling", "thinking", "hearing"), then return to the primary object; move to slow walking with labels for lifting, moving and placing.

natural-awareness-right-attitude.name: Natural awareness (right attitude)
natural-awareness-right-attitude.summary: Instead of forcing focus on one object, relax and know whatever is being experienced, checking the attitude of the observing mind (craving, aversion, impatience) throughout daily activities.

steps.text: Instead of forcing focus on one object, relax and know whatever is being experienced, checking the attitude of the observing mind (craving, aversion, impatience) throughout daily activities.

satipatthana-four-establishings-of-mindf.name: Satipaṭṭhāna (four establishings of mindfulness)
satipatthana-four-establishings-of-mindf.summary: Contemplate body, feeling, mind and mental qualities as they arise and pass, ardent, clearly knowing and mindful, without greed or distress about the world (MN 10).

steps.text: Contemplate body, feeling, mind and mental qualities as they arise and pass, ardent, clearly knowing and mindful, without greed or distress about the world (MN 10).

rain.name: RAIN
rain.summary: Recognise what is happening; Allow it to be there; Investigate with kindness how it feels in the body; Nurture with self-compassion; then rest in the awareness that remains.

steps.text: Recognise what is happening; Allow it to be there; Investigate with kindness how it feels in the body; Nurture with self-compassion; then rest in the awareness that remains.

open-awareness-shamatha-without-a-suppor.name: Open awareness (shamatha without a support)
open-awareness-shamatha-without-a-suppor.summary: After a few minutes with a support, let it go. Leave the eyes open and the gaze soft. Let sights, sounds and thoughts come and go, and do not follow them or push them away. When you get caught up, simply notice it and relax again. The point is to rest as the knowing that is already present.

looking-at-the-mind-mahamudra.name: Looking at the mind (Mahamudra)
looking-at-the-mind-mahamudra.summary: Once the mind is calm, turn and look for the one who is looking. Ask where a thought comes from, where it stays, and where it goes. Do not reason about it; just look and rest in whatever is seen or not found. This practice is traditionally done under a qualified teacher's guidance.

resting-in-rigpa-dzogchen-orientation-on.name: Resting in rigpa (Dzogchen), orientation only
resting-in-rigpa-dzogchen-orientation-on.summary: In Dzogchen, the student is introduced to the nature of mind (rigpa) by a teacher. Between sessions, practitioners recall that recognition, leave it uncontrived for short moments, many times, and release any effort to improve it. This entry describes the practice and is not a substitute for the introduction itself.

steps.text: In Dzogchen, the student is introduced to the nature of mind (rigpa) by a teacher. This entry describes the practice and is not a substitute for the introduction itself.

shikantaza-just-sitting.name: Shikantaza (just sitting)
shikantaza-just-sitting.summary: Sit as in zazen, but drop counting and any object. Simply sit, aware of the whole posture and the whole field of experience, without chasing or suppressing anything. When you find yourself lost in thought, come back to the posture. Dogen treats the sitting itself as realisation, not as a means to it.

koan-practice-with-mu.name: Koan practice with Mu
koan-practice-with-mu.summary: Take up "Does a dog have buddha nature? Mu" (Zhaozhou). Breathe Mu on each exhalation and put your whole doubt into it. Do not interpret it. Present your understanding to a teacher in private interview (dokusan). Koan work depends on that meeting with a teacher.

silent-illumination-mozhao.name: Silent illumination (mozhao)
silent-illumination-mozhao.summary: Relax the body and be aware of the whole body sitting. Widen that awareness to include the environment, without any centre or edge. Silence means not adding commentary; illumination means remaining clearly aware. Rest there, and return whenever you get caught.

steps.text: Relax the body and be aware of the whole body sitting.

bhairavi-sadhana-isha.name: Bhairavi Sadhana (Isha)
bhairavi-sadhana-isha.summary: A lay devotional observance offered by the Isha Foundation around Linga Bhairavi: for a set period the practitioner keeps simple disciplines (as given by Isha), offers daily devotion to the goddess, and completes it with an offering at a Linga Bhairavi abode. The exact rules come from the organisation each year.

sravana-manana-nididhyasana.name: Śravaṇa–manana–nididhyāsana
sravana-manana-nididhyasana.summary: Systematic listening to the Upaniṣads with a teacher (śravaṇa), resolving doubts by reflection (manana), and dwelling on the understood meaning until it is assimilated (nididhyāsana).

steps.text: Systematic listening to the Upaniṣads with a teacher (śravaṇa), resolving doubts by reflection (manana), and dwelling on the understood meaning until it is assimilated (nididhyāsana).

japa-repetition-of-a-divine-name.name: Japa (repetition of a divine name)
japa-repetition-of-a-divine-name.summary: Repeat a mantra or name of God given by the teacher, often with a mālā of 108 beads, letting the mind rest in its meaning and the feeling of devotion.

steps.text: Repeat a mantra or name of God given by the teacher, often with a mālā of 108 beads, letting the mind rest in its meaning and the feeling of devotion.

hare-krishna-mahamantra-japa-and-kirtan.name: Hare Krishna mahāmantra (japa and kīrtan)
hare-krishna-mahamantra-japa-and-kirtan.summary: Chant "Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare / Hare Rāma Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma Hare Hare" softly on beads (japa) or sing it together (kīrtan), as practised since Chaitanya.

steps.text: Chant "Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare / Hare Rāma Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma Hare Hare" softly on beads (japa) or sing it together (kīrtan), as practised since Chaitanya.

nembutsu-nianfo.name: Nembutsu / nianfo
nembutsu-nianfo.summary: Recite "Namu Amida Butsu" (Japanese) or "Namo Amituofo" (Chinese), aloud or silently, with a mala if you like. In Chinese Pure Land, recitation is a practice of concentration and aspiration for rebirth. In Shin Buddhism, it is an expression of gratitude for Amida's vow, not a means of earning anything.

christian-meditation-with-a-mantra-maran.name: Christian meditation with a mantra (Maranatha)
christian-meditation-with-a-mantra-maran.summary: Sit still and upright with your eyes lightly closed. Silently repeat one prayer-word, "Ma-ra-na-tha", in four equal syllables, listening to it rather than thinking about its meaning. When thoughts or images arrive, return to the word, without force. Sit for 20–30 minutes, morning and evening.

centering-prayer.name: Centering Prayer
centering-prayer.summary: Choose a sacred word as a sign of consent to God's presence. Sit comfortably and bring it in gently. When you notice you are engaged with a thought, return ever so gently to the word. End by resting in silence for a couple of minutes. Twice daily, 20 minutes.

steps.text: Choose a sacred word as a sign of consent to God's presence.

When you notice you are engaged with a thought, return ever so gently to the word.
End by resting in silence for a couple of minutes.
Twice daily, 20 minutes.

lectio-divina.name: Lectio Divina
lectio-divina.summary: Read a short scripture passage slowly, then again; notice the word that catches you; respond to it in prayer; rest in silence. Read, ponder, pray, rest.

steps.text: Read a short scripture passage slowly, then again; notice the word that catches you; respond to it in prayer; rest in silence.
Read, ponder, pray, rest.

the-jesus-prayer-prayer-of-the-heart.name: The Jesus Prayer (prayer of the heart)
the-jesus-prayer-prayer-of-the-heart.summary: Repeat "Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me" slowly and attentively, often with a prayer rope, keeping the mind in the words and letting it descend into the heart. Begin with a fixed time each day; humility and stillness come before technique.

steps.text: Repeat "Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me" slowly and attentively, often with a prayer rope, keeping the mind in the words and letting it descend into the heart.

zikr-remembrance-in-the-inayati-way.name: Zikr (remembrance) in the Inayati way
zikr-remembrance-in-the-inayati-way.summary: Sitting quietly, repeat the phrase of divine unity (La ilaha illa'llah) aloud or silently, letting the breath and a gentle movement of the head carry it, until the remembrance continues on its own in the heart.

steps.text: Sitting quietly, repeat the phrase of divine unity (La ilaha illa'llah) aloud or silently, letting the breath and a gentle movement of the head carry it, until the remembrance continues on its own in the heart.

contraindications: Keep the breath natural and unforced. Stop if you feel dizzy, anxious or unwell.

dhikr-and-breathwork.name: Dhikr and breathwork
dhikr-and-breathwork.summary: Join a short divine name or phrase to the in- and out-breath; keep attention on the heart; finish with silence and a prayer.

steps.text: Join a short divine name or phrase to the in- and out-breath; keep attention on the heart; finish with silence and a prayer.
